- If sentiment is consistently bullish (≥0.7) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.
- If sentiment is bearish (≤0.3) and price has recently spiked, model often overshoots downward; cap forecast decline at 2–5% below peak.
- When sentiment flips sharply from bullish to bearish, model lags in adjusting downward; apply 1–2 day lag correction to downward moves.
- If model forecast mean is > true mean by >5%, consider mean reversion bias; reduce forecast by 0.5–1.5% per day until convergence.
- For 30-day horizon, if true outcome shows early sharp drop after spike, model often fails to anticipate; add 1–2 day buffer for downward correction.
- If sentiment history shows high volatility (alternating 0.5–1.0), model overfits short-term noise; smooth forecast with 3–5 day moving average.
